1  # Write the Hook Code
   2  We need to create a new plugin directory under pkg/rules/ and then write the plugin code, like this:
   3  
   4  ```go
   5  package mux
   6  
   7  import _ "unsafe"
   8  import "github.com/alibaba/loongsuite-go/pkg/api"
   9  import mux "github.com/gorilla/mux"
  10  
  11  //go:linkname muxRoute130OnEnter github.com/gorilla/mux.muxRoute130OnEnter
  12  func muxRoute130OnEnter(call api.CallContext, req *http.Request, route interface{}) {
  13      ...
  14  }
  15  ```
  16  There's no magic here — it's just regular Go code. A few interesting points:
  17  
  18  - The hook function muxRoute130OnEnter must be annotated with the go:linkname directive.
  19  - The first parameter of the hook function must be of type api.CallContext, and the remaining parameters should match those of the target function:
  20    - If the target function is `func foo(a int, b string, c float) (d string, e error)`, then the onEnter hook function should be `func hook(call api.CallContext, a int, b string, c float)`
  21    - If the target function is `func foo(a int, b string, c float) (d string, e error)`, then the onExit hook function should be `func hook(call api.CallContext, d string, e error)`
  22    - If you need to modify the parameters or return values of the target function, you can use `CallContext.SetParam()` or `CallContext.SetReturnVal()`
  23  
  24  We need more documentation explaining all aspects of writing plugin code. For now, the best way is to refer to other plugin implementations, such as `pkg/rules/mux` or any other existing plugin.

1  # Compatibility
   2  
   3  `loongsuite-go` ensures compatibility with the current supported
   4  versions of
   5  the [Go language](https://golang.org/doc/devel/release#policy):
   6  
   7  > Each major Go release is supported until there are two newer major releases.
   8  > For example, Go 1.5 was supported until the Go 1.7 release, and Go 1.6 was supported until the Go 1.8 release.
   9  
  10  For versions of Go that are no longer supported upstream, `loongsuite-go` will
  11  stop ensuring compatibility with these versions in the following manner:
  12  
  13  - A minor release of `loongsuite-go` will be made to add support for the new
  14  supported release of Go.
  15  - The following minor release of `loongsuite-go` will remove compatibility
  16  testing for the oldest (now archived upstream) version of Go. This, and
  17  future, releases of `loongsuite-go` may include features only supported by
  18  the currently supported versions of Go.
  19  
  20  > [!IMPORTANT]
  21  > **Minimum Go version: 1.25.** Since OpenTelemetry v1.42.0 the OTel modules
  22  > declare `go 1.25.0`, and `loongsuite-go` pins OTel v1.45.0. Because the tool
  23  > injects those modules into the application it instruments, both the tool and
  24  > the instrumented application require Go 1.25 or newer. A Go 1.24 build only
  25  > keeps working because the default `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` silently downloads a
  26  > 1.25 toolchain; with `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` it fails.
  27  
  28  This project is tested on the following systems.
  29  
  30  | OS       | Go Version | Architecture |
  31  | -------- | ---------- | ------------ |
